claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children are you wanting to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm wanting to claim for one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17 years old - he was born in March 2007.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's useful information.

Let me check the specific eligibility rules to make sure I understand the requirements correctly for his situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, this is actually good news for you!

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex is 17, has just left school, and has signed up with the local careers service, this means **you would be eligible for Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks** from the date he registered with the careers service.

Before I confirm this as my final assessment, I need to ask one more important question:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex (either living with him and/or paying towards his upkeep such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

I have all the information I need to provide you with my assessment. Let me summarize the key points:

- Alex is 17 years old (born March 2007)
- He has recently left school
- He has registered with the local careers service
- He lives at home with you
- You are responsible for him

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex for a period of **up to 20 weeks** from the date he registered with the careers service. This is a special provision that applies when a young person aged 16 or 17 leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!**

You should now be in a position to claim. The eligibility runs for up to 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. If you haven't already applied, you can do so through the official government channels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?
